subject: E-sign vendor consolidation: recommended approach and approvals
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@ironclad.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@docusign.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: E-sign vendor consolidation: key questions and schedule

Hi team / partners —

We ran a quick review across last quarter's e-sign usage and costs. Attached is a lightweight chart (20261118-esign-costs.xlsx) showing volume by product line and the top 10 customers by envelope/API spend. Goal: consolidate primary signing flows to a single vendor where it reduces unit cost and operational toil, but keep a fallback (API-compatible) capability for compliance/regional requirements.

High-level asks for vendors (Alicia, Ben):
- Confirm API bulk-send throughput and sustained parallel signing limits (our busiest flows hit ~2500 envelopes/hr).
- Confirm support for SAML SSO + JIT provisioning for external partners and for per-tenant branding.
- Clarify retention of auditable acceptance records and export formats (we need tamper-evident PDFs + raw event logs for 7 years).
- Data residency options for EU workloads (we have GDPR customers where signing must remain in eu-west-1).
- Any discounts for committed volumes + multi-product bundles, and contract term flexibility for staged migration.

Internal ask: Marissa/Markus, can you review the attached cost spreadsheet and note any procurement constraints? Laura — can you sanity-check the capex/opex split if we pursue a reserved capacity model?

Timeline proposal: vendor answers by EOD Thu 11/19; internal recommendation and cost scenario by Fri 11/20; executive ask (if needed) the afternoon of 11/20.

Thanks —

—Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: E-sign vendor consolidation: key questions and schedule

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from Ironclad side (we're happy to provide more detail and a short demo if useful):

- Throughput: our managed cluster supports sustained throughput of 3k envelopes/hr for single-tenant production workloads; we can provision burst capacity above that for a 24-48h window. We recommend a soft concurrency ceiling (per-tenant) to avoid head-of-line latencies.
- SSO/JIT: Full SAML 2.0 support with OKTA + Azure AD integrations; JIT provisioning supported with custom claims mapping.
- Audit records: We provide tamper-evident PDFs, and an event log export (JSON) with chained signatures. Standard retention is 3 years; we offer extended retention up to 7 years via an add-on.
- EU residency: We have infrastructure in eu-west-1 and can guarantee signing data residency for specific orgs (requires DPA + addendum).
- Pricing: We can offer a two-tier committed-volume discount (12–24 month) and waive integration fees for partnerships on multi-year commitments.

I've attached our KBA with API rate limits and recommended batching patterns (ironclad-kba.pdf).

If helpful, I can set up a 30-minute tech sync with our product engineer tomorrow morning to walk through the bulk-send pattern.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Enterprise Sales Engineering, Ironclad
agomez@ironclad.com

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: E-sign vendor consolidation: key questions and schedule

Hi Stephanie & team —

Appreciate the note. DocuSign's quick responses below:

- Throughput: our recommended enterprise config supports sustained 5k envelopes/hr with optimal parallelization; we also have priority lanes for high-volume customers. We typically tune rate limits per contract.
- SSO + provisioning: SAML + SCIM provisioning supported; we can also provide an org-level admin sync for partner orgs.
- Audit trail: Long-term archival in WORM storage; we can export both signed PDFs and CSV/JSON event logs.
- EU residency: We have EU-local signing and a dedicated EU tenant option (requires a separate contract and backing infrastructure).
- Migration: We have a migration toolkit and can absorb a portion of migration costs for >= 12-month commitments.

I attached a short API performance note (esign-api-performance.pdf) that shows parallel envelope patterns and common pitfalls. Happy to join Alicia for the tech sync if you want a cross-vendor session.

Cheers,
Ben Turner
Strategic Accounts, DocuSign
ben.turner@docusign.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: E-sign vendor consolidation: key questions and schedule

Marissa / Markus / Laura —

Thanks to both vendors for the rapid responses. I summarized the key decision points below after reviewing the attachments and chatting with engineering:

Executive summary (recommendation):
- Primary vendor: DocuSign for high-volume customer flows (best sustained throughput and EU tenant option).
- Secondary/fallback: Ironclad for workflow-heavy, template-driven legal intake where deeper CLM hooks matter (their event logs and KBA look solid).
- Migration approach: phased — migrate 70% transactional envelopes to DocuSign with a 9–12 month runway; keep Ironclad for CLM-integrated flows and legal team templates (ongoing).
- Licensing: pursue a committed volume discount with DocuSign (12–24 months) and negotiate Ironclad retention add-on for long-term archival pricing.

Risks & mitigations:
- Data residency for EU customers: require explicit EU tenant in DocuSign contract and DPA addendum — Marissa, please flag any required contract language.
- Audit retention: confirm export formats and a quarterly validation test for event logs — Laura, ops cost estimate attached.
- Budget: projected incremental opex in year 1 but 18% unit-cost savings by year 2 if we hit commit thresholds (see sheet).

Approve to proceed? If yes, I will:
1) Draft a short commercial term sheet for DocuSign and loop in procurement for SOW/PO creation.
2) Request a formal Ironclad addendum for archive retention and CLM integration SLAs.
3) Schedule a 30-min exec readout Mon 11/23 (if needed).

Please reply with APPROVE / QUESTIONS by EOD Mon 11/22. If I don't hear objections, I'll start term-sheet drafting.

—Stephanie
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
